note.justification: For transport, expand an arbitrary vector after applying the linear isomorphism in the given basis and apply its inverse; a relation among the transported vectors maps to a relation in that basis, hence all coefficients vanish. For reduction, write u uniquely as the finite sum Σ a_i b e_i. Its class vanishes iff u=pw; expansion of w proves all a_i are multiples of p, and conversely such coefficients give u=pΣ d_i b e_i. Thus residue coordinates exist uniquely, and B takes (b e_i)⊗1 to [b e_i]⊗1. This is an explicit finite-coordinate check of the exact transports in S003; no additional freeness or quotient-basis theorem is assumed.
